title: Where are you on the scale?
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: On a scale of one to ten, where are you as an all-in entrepreneur?

Part of this journey is being comfortable with crisis situations, especially when you're doing something new, I said. As you get older you mitigate your risk more and take less risk. But your nature as an entrepreneur is to see value before anybody else.

We see entrepreneurs who bail, I said: they raise money and leave investors hanging. A core thing is: somebody invests in you, puts their faith in you. If you have that fortitude, those people stay through thick and thin. It's do or die, until you make it.
Because you made it once doesn't mean you will make it again, I said. A lot of us make that mistake: I had success, it will be easier. It's not.
A student said: some people stop doing the things that got them there, and if you lose that foundation it's hard to sustain the growth.
We are always driven by fear, I said, which isn't a bad thing. That fear has to become vigilance: due diligence, paying attention, hyper-focus. It has to be consistent and relentless.

groups.heading: Where are you on the scale?

lines.text: A student said the person has the exact personality type of an entrepreneur: black or white, a hundred percent in or out. I said: on a scale of one to ten, he is at a nine or ten. Where are we? A two, a three, a four? Where are we comfortable? Am I too comfortable? Am I not pushing enough?
How much do I influence the people around me? I asked. Am I inspirational? What is my tone of voice, my enthusiasm? Are people looking at me thinking: this person is mission-driven, at all costs?
It's about being so aware of where you are and how you create standards for yourself, I said. He has a standard, and an immense, positive self-belief, and doesn't waver from it even through the pain.
Where are you on the scale, and are you comfortable there?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write where you are on the one-to-ten scale and why.
Write whether you are too comfortable.
Write what your tone and enthusiasm do to your team.
Write the standard you set yourself.
Write one thing that got you here that you must keep doing.

check.q: What did I say about having succeeded once?
choices: It doesn't mean you will make it again
It makes the next time easy

check.q: What did I say fear should become?

choices: One to ten, from comfortable to all-in

recap: Know where you are on the scale. Turn fear into vigilance. Keep doing what got you here.
